publication.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025

name: Explorer: Scaling Exploration-driven Web Trajectory Synthesis for Multimodal Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Synthesizes multimodal web trajectories through exploration and refinement, then trains a browser agent to study the effect of scaling interaction data.

name: UXAgent: An LLM Agent-Based Usability Testing Framework for Web Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The system is intended to help researchers refine study designs before conducting studies with human participants.
summary: Introduces UXAgent, which uses simulated users and a browser connector to test website usability and present their actions, responses, and recordings to UX researchers.

name: WebGames: Challenging General-Purpose Web-Browsing AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported comparisons are from the benchmark's interactive challenges.
summary: Introduces WebGames, a browser-agent benchmark with 50+ interactive challenges in a self-contained test environment and verifiable solutions.

name: Why Are Web AI Agents More Vulnerable Than Standalone LLMs? A Security Analysis
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Analyzes web-agent vulnerabilities at the component level, examining goal placement in prompts, multistep action generation, and observations as sources of increased susceptibility.

publication.title: LiteWebAgent: The Open-Source Suite for VLM-Based Web-Agent Applications
publication.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (System Demonstrations)

name: LiteWebAgent: The Open-Source Suite for VLM-Based Web-Agent Applications
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a modular visual web-agent stack with planning and memory components, exposed through a remote-browser application and Chrome extension.

name: BEARCUBS: A benchmark for computer-using web agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: BEARCUBS provides 111 live-web information-seeking questions with short answers and human-validated browsing trajectories. Its tasks require multimodal computer interaction, including video understanding and navigation of interactive 3D content.

name: WebNav: An Intelligent Agent for Voice-Controlled Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract presents the system architecture and implementation.
summary: Introduces WebNav, a web navigation agent that turns natural-language commands into GUI actions using screenshot context, DOM labels, and separate LLMs for planning and action parameters.

name: A Survey of WebAgents: Towards Next-Generation AI Agents for Web Automation with Large Foundation Models
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: Surveys foundation-model web agents through their architectures, training methods and trustworthiness. It organizes research on completing browser tasks from user instructions and identifies directions for further development.

name: An Illusion of Progress? Assessing the Current State of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Online-Mind2Web, with 300 tasks across 136 live websites, and examines how benchmark design affects assessments of web agents. It also develops an LLM judge for task completion and compares its judgments with human evaluation.

name: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Adapts web agents to execute natural-language test steps, verify assertions, and issue test verdicts. The study introduces 113 passing and failing test cases across three offline web applications and compares two agent implementations with qualitative failure analysis.

name: Inducing Programmatic Skills for Agentic Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract evaluates ASI on WebArena and examines skill transfer between websites.
summary: Introduces agent skill induction (ASI), which creates, checks, and reuses program-based skills for web tasks by combining primitive actions into higher-level routines.

name: SkillWeaver: Web Agents can Self-Improve by Discovering and Honing Skills
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SkillWeaver explores websites, practices interactions, and converts the resulting experience into a reusable library of callable skill APIs. Its WebArena and live-website experiments examine skill refinement, composition, and transfer from stronger agents to weaker ones.

name: AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AgentRewardBench evaluates automated web-agent judges against expert reviews of 1,302 trajectories from five benchmarks. The annotations cover completion, side effects, and repetition, enabling comparison of LLM judges and rule-based task evaluators.

name: AgentA/B: Automated and Scalable Web A/BTesting with Interactive LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4). The abstract describes a controlled shopping-site experiment comparing simulated agents with human behavior.
summary: Introduces AgentA/B, which uses persona-based LLM agents to navigate real webpages and perform shopping interactions for simulated web A/B tests.

name: REAL: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Deterministic Simulations of Real Websites
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). All evaluated interactions occur in controlled simulations of websites.
summary: Introduces REAL, a benchmark of deterministic website replicas with 112 tasks covering information retrieval and state-changing browser actions.

name: WebRollback: Enhancing Web Agents with Explicit Rollback Mechanisms
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebRollback gives a web agent an explicit action for returning to an earlier state in its navigation trajectory. It studies this recovery mechanism on two live web-navigation benchmarks under both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings.

name: WebLists: Extracting Structured Information From Complex Interactive Websites Using Executable LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark covers data extraction across four business and enterprise use cases.
summary: Introduces WebLists, a benchmark for structured extraction from interactive websites, and BardeenAgent, which turns web-agent runs into replayable CSS-selector programs.

name: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WASP, an end-to-end benchmark for prompt-injection security in web agents. Its evaluation separates partial attack progress from completion of the attacker’s full objective.

name: WebEvolver: Enhancing Web Agent Self-Improvement with Coevolving World Model
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WebEvolver trains a co-evolving world model to predict web observations and generate additional agent-training trajectories. The same model supports look-ahead action selection at inference, with evaluation on live web-task benchmarks.

name: WebThinker: Empowering Large Reasoning Models with Deep Research Capability
notes: Adjacent web-research method. The retained abstract and full-text Section 3 and Appendix A describe search APIs and Crawl4AI URL retrieval; no visual GUI execution is inferred.
summary: Combines iterative web search and link-following with interleaved reasoning and report drafting for deep research. Its reported web explorer retrieves page content through a crawler rather than controlling a visual browser interface.

name: Visual Test-time Scaling for GUI Agent Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RegionFocus adds visual test-time scaling by zooming into selected screenshot regions and maintaining an image-based map of landmarks and actions. It evaluates this grounding procedure with UI-TARS and Qwen2.5-VL on ScreenSpot-Pro and WebVoyager.

name: WebGen-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Generating Interactive and Functional Websites from Scratch
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark targets website code generation; browser navigation is used to test the generated sites.
summary: Introduces WebGen-Bench for evaluating agents that generate multi-file websites, using a web-navigation agent to check whether the resulting pages pass interaction tests.

name: AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4). The framework targets LLM agents broadly; web navigation is one attack outcome reported in the abstract.
summary: Introduces AgentVigil, a black-box fuzzing framework for finding indirect prompt injections against LLM agents, including attacks that redirect web navigation.

name: WebInject: Prompt Injection Attack to Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4).
summary: Introduces WebInject, a prompt-injection attack that optimizes rendered webpage pixels to make screenshot-based web agents take attacker-chosen actions.

name: The Hidden Dangers of Browsing AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Outlines an end-to-end threat model and empirical security evaluation across architectural layers of autonomous browser agents.

name: Web-Shepherd: Advancing PRMs for Reinforcing Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Web-Shepherd is a process reward model for assessing individual steps of web-navigation trajectories. It introduces a collection of 40,000 step-level preference pairs with checklists and a separate benchmark for comparing reward models, then evaluates verification during WebArena-lite navigation.

name: WebAgent-R1: Training Web Agents via End-to-End Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Trains web agents through asynchronous multi-turn environment interaction, using task-success rewards to optimize complete trajectories.

name: WebCoT: Enhancing Web Agent Reasoning by Reconstructing Chain-of-Thought in Reflection, Branching, and Rollback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WebCoT turns reflection, look-ahead, branching and rollback procedures into chain-of-thought training rationales. Fine-tuning on these reconstructed trajectories is evaluated for web-agent self-improvement and transfer across navigation tasks.

name: AdInject: Real-World Black-Box Attacks on Web Agents via Advertising Delivery
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies advertising delivery as an indirect-injection channel for web agents under a black-box threat model. AdInject evaluates how static ad content shaped by website context can redirect browser actions.

name: Open CaptchaWorld: A Comprehensive Web-based Platform for Testing and Benchmarking Multimodal LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: Open CaptchaWorld evaluates multimodal agents on interactive browser-based CAPTCHA puzzles. Its benchmark distinguishes task success from the depth of visual reasoning and interaction needed to complete a puzzle.

name: ResTest: Targeted Coverage of Residual Not-Covered Code Using Large Language Models for Web GUI Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its reported coverage results come from ten open-source web applications.
summary: Introduces ResTest, which uses coverage reports and a state transition graph to infer untested web functions, then directs a GUI agent to execute them.

name: WebChoreArena: Evaluating Web Browsing Agents on Realistic Tedious Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces WebChoreArena, 532 web chores built on WebArena environments to evaluate agents’ retention of page information, calculation, and tracking across pages.

name: DeepShop: A Benchmark for Deep Research Shopping Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: DeepShop evaluates shopping agents with evolving query complexity across product attributes, filters and sorting preferences. Its evaluation combines checks of these individual requirements with overall task success.

name: Surfer-H Meets Holo1: Cost-Efficient Web Agent Powered by Open Weights
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes Surfer-H, a web agent paired with the Holo1 vision-language model family trained on web content, synthetic examples, and agent-generated data. The work introduces WebClick for web-interface localization and evaluates browser task execution on WebVoyager.

name: Go-Browse: Training Web Agents with Structured Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Go-Browse frames web-environment exploration as graph search so that information can be reused across data-collection episodes. It collects 10,000 successful trajectories and 40,000 interaction steps on WebArena and uses them to fine-tune a web agent.

name: Thinking vs. Doing: Agents that Reason by Scaling Test-Time Interaction
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: Test-Time Interaction scales the interaction horizon so web agents can explore, backtrack and revise plans within a rollout. Its online reinforcement-learning curriculum adjusts rollout lengths and is evaluated on WebVoyager and WebArena.

name: EconWebArena: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Economic Tasks in Realistic Web Environments
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Introduces EconWebArena, a curated benchmark of economic-data tasks requiring live website navigation, multimodal interpretation, and precise extraction. It evaluates visual grounding, planning, and interaction design within multistep workflows.

name: Mirage-1: Augmenting and Updating GUI Agent with Hierarchical Multimodal Skills
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Mirage-1 organizes interaction trajectories into execution, core, and meta-skills, then uses them to guide Monte Carlo tree search during online GUI tasks. It introduces AndroidLH for long-horizon evaluation and tests the approach on Android and web-navigation benchmarks.

name: Build the web for agents, not agents for the web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). This is a position paper proposing interface design principles.
summary: Proposes Agentic Web Interface (AWI), a website interface intended for agent navigation, and sets out six design principles for web-agent use.

name: Embodied Web Agents: Bridging Physical-Digital Realms for Integrated Agent Intelligence
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The physical component is a simulation; the supported catalog connection is its functional web interaction.
summary: Introduces environments that couple 3D physical-world simulations with functional web interfaces. The accompanying benchmark evaluates tasks requiring agents to coordinate online information and physical actions across cooking, navigation and shopping scenarios.

name: Mind2Web 2: Evaluating Agentic Search with Agent-as-a-Judge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark assesses agentic search answers and source attribution.
summary: Introduces Mind2Web 2, 130 long-horizon tasks requiring live web browsing and information synthesis, plus an Agent-as-a-Judge framework for grading answers and sources.

name: LineRetriever: Planning-Aware Observation Reduction for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LineRetriever uses a language model to select observation lines that matter for upcoming web-navigation actions. It reduces DOM or accessibility-tree context by considering the planning horizon instead of relying solely on semantic similarity.

name: WebArxiv: A Reproducible Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Web Agents on arXiv Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebArxiv provides 510 static-snapshot tasks with deterministic answers for scholarly browsing, including constrained paper retrieval, content extraction, and cross-paper comparison. The study also tests dynamic retrieval of interaction history to address repetitive or incomplete agent reasoning.

name: Less is More: Empowering GUI Agent with Context-Aware Simplification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SimpAgent prunes distracting interface elements with visual masks and compresses interaction history using consistency-based guidance. The study evaluates these two forms of context reduction during GUI navigation in web and mobile environments.

name: WebSynthesis: World-Model-Guided MCTS for Efficient WebUI-Trajectory Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its trajectory generation takes place in simulated virtual web environments.
summary: Introduces WebSynthesis, which uses a learned web world model and tree-based planning to synthesize interaction trajectories for training web agents.

name: R-VLM: Region-Aware Vision Language Model for Precise GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: R-VLM localizes GUI elements through zoomed-in region proposals and an intersection-over-union-aware training objective. It evaluates the grounding model on ScreenSpot and AgentStudio and studies its effect on navigation in AITW and Mind2Web.

name: Let's Think in Two Steps: Mitigating Agreement Bias in MLLMs with Self-Grounded Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The verifier study also covers robotics, beyond web and computer-use agents.
summary: Studies agreement bias in multimodal agent verifiers across web navigation and computer use, and introduces SGV to assess trajectories using self-generated priors.

name: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via HTML Accessibility Tree
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies indirect prompt injection through HTML content consumed as accessibility trees. The evaluation tests how manipulated page observations redirect browser-agent actions on real websites.

name: Magentic-UI: Towards Human-in-the-loop Agentic Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Magentic-UI combines browser interaction, code execution, file operations, and MCP tools in an interface for human-agent collaboration. It studies collaborative planning and task execution, action guards, and persistent memory through benchmark tasks, simulated users, user studies, and safety assessments.

name: General Agentic Planning Through Simulative Reasoning with World Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Evaluation covers three task categories within a web-browser environment.
summary: Introduces SiRA, an agent architecture that uses a language-based world model to simulate action outcomes for planning in web-browser tasks.

name: Web-CogReasoner: Towards Multimodal Knowledge-Induced Cognitive Reasoning for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Web-CogReasoner separates factual and conceptual web knowledge from procedural reasoning, using a structured curriculum to train a multimodal agent. Web-CogDataset and Web-CogBench support study of these capabilities alongside web-navigation evaluation.

name: HarmonyGuard: Toward Safety and Utility in Web Agents via Adaptive Policy Enhancement and Dual-Objective Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported policy-compliance and task-completion gains are from the paper’s benchmark evaluations.
summary: Introduces HarmonyGuard, a multi-agent framework that updates security policies and weighs safety against task completion for agents operating on the open web.

name: Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: D2Snap reduces serialized DOM observations while preserving actionable elements and features that distinguish their uses. The study compares reduced DOM inputs with screenshot-based observations for a web agent on tasks sampled from Online-Mind2Web.

name: Cognitive Duality for Adaptive Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces CogniWeb, which switches between fast reactive processing and slower deliberative reasoning according to task complexity. WebArena experiments examine this combination of learned behaviors and online planning.

name: WebMall -- A Multi-Shop Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebMall provides four simulated online shops with heterogeneous product data for comparison shopping, related-product searches, and checkout tasks. It evaluates web agents with different observation formats and memory configurations in a fixed offline environment.

name: MM-BrowseComp: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Browsing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MM-BrowseComp, a benchmark for browsing agents that must use evidence from web images and videos to answer multimodal search questions.

name: A Functionality-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents in E-commerce Domains
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Amazon-Bench generates functionality-specific web tasks from page content and interactive controls, covering operations beyond product search. Its evaluator checks task completion and unintended changes to account state, such as address or purchase settings.

name: WebSight: A Vision-First Architecture for Robust Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebSight uses a vision-language model trained on web-interface examples within a modular agent with planning, action, verification, and episodic memory components. It evaluates element clicking on Showdown Clicks and full browsing tasks on WebVoyager using visual observations.

name: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Introduces Morae, a UI agent that detects decision points and pauses for user choices using interface code and screenshots. A study with blind and low-vision participants evaluates this mixed-initiative approach on real web tasks.

name: MMSearch-Plus: Benchmarking Provenance-Aware Search for Multimodal Browsing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces MMSearch-Plus, a multimodal browsing benchmark with iterative image-text search, and an agent framework that marks and crops images for targeted retrieval.

name: PrivWeb: Unobtrusive and Content-aware Privacy Protection For Web Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces PrivWeb, which uses a local language model to anonymize interface information according to user preferences. Adaptive notifications and selective pauses give users control over sensitive information access during web-agent tasks.

name: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces ReSum, which compresses interaction histories during long web searches, and ReSum-GRPO, which trains agents to reason across the resulting segments.

name: TGPO: Tree-Guided Preference Optimization for Robust Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: TGPO merges semantically equivalent web states into tree-structured trajectories for offline preference optimization. A process reward model scores subgoal progress, redundant behavior, and action validity, while dynamic weighting emphasizes consequential decisions.

name: Detecting Pipeline Failures through Fine-Grained Analysis of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a modular framework for identifying errors at intermediate stages of a web-agent pipeline. A SeeAct and Mind2Web case study examines weaknesses that are obscured by final task-success metrics.

name: Recon-Act: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Browser-Use System via Web Reconnaissance, Tool Generation, and Task Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract says the implementation has reached Level 3 of its proposed roadmap, with limited human intervention.
summary: Introduces Recon-Act, a browser-use framework that compares failed and successful web trajectories to create reusable tools for planning and executing long-horizon website tasks.

name: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: RAG-GUI trains a small guidance adapter to filter and summarize retrieved web tutorials while keeping the acting agent fixed. Supervised and rejection-sampling stages prepare the adapter for inference-time assistance, tested on offline web/mobile tasks and interactive Android tasks.

name: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Distills generalizable reasoning strategies from both successful and failed agent trajectories into a persistent memory bank for test-time retrieval.

name: Graph2Eval: Automatic Multimodal Task Generation for Agents via Knowledge Graphs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The framework also generates document-understanding tasks for RAG agents.
summary: Introduces Graph2Eval, which generates multimodal agent evaluation tasks from knowledge graphs, including multi-step web interactions in Graph2Eval-Bench.

name: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.

name: BrowserArena: Evaluating LLM Agents on Real-World Web Navigation Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces BrowserArena, a live-web platform for head-to-head agent comparisons on user-submitted tasks. Step-level human annotations support targeted analysis of navigation, pop-up handling and CAPTCHA-related failures.

name: WAREX: Web Agent Reliability Evaluation on Existing Benchmarks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WAREX augments existing web-agent benchmarks with reliability challenges arising from unstable systems and changing or disruptive website behavior. Evaluation on WebArena, WebVoyager and REAL examines how these disturbances affect task completion.

name: Cross-Modal Content Optimization for Steering Web Agent Preferences
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The attacker can edit only their own listing's images and textual metadata.
summary: Introduces Cross-Modal Preference Steering (CPS), a black-box attack that edits a listing's images and text to steer VLM-based web agents' selections.

name: JEF-Hinter: Leveraging Offline Knowledge for Improving Web Agents Adaptation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces JEF-Hinter, which distills successful and failed trajectories into compact episodic hints and retrieves them for the current agent state. Web benchmark experiments examine guidance from decisive steps rather than full demonstration replay.

name: WARC-Bench: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WARC-Bench packages dynamic web pages as replayable archives and evaluates short navigation subtasks involving components such as date pickers and scrollable containers. It also studies supervised training followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on these browser interactions.

name: BrowserAgent: Building Web Agents with Human-Inspired Web Browsing Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains BrowserAgent to use Playwright-based scrolling, clicking and typing directly on webpages for information-seeking tasks. Supervised and rejection fine-tuning are paired with explicit memory for conclusions carried across steps.

name: WebRouter: Query-specific Router via Variational Information Bottleneck for Cost-sensitive Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Experiments cover five websites from WebVoyager.
summary: Introduces WebRouter, a cost-aware router that compresses web-agent prompts to choose among LLMs, with cost and accuracy measured on WebVoyager websites.

name: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HackWorld for evaluating visual computer-use agents in a capture-the-flag collection of web applications. The benchmark examines interface navigation and multistep planning during vulnerability discovery and exploitation tasks.

name: WebAggregator: Enhancing Compositional Reasoning Capabilities of Deep Research Agent Foundation Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The work centers on research questions and evidence aggregation across websites.
summary: Introduces WebAggregator, a pipeline for synthesizing compositional questions from websites to train deep-research agents, plus the WebAggregatorQA testbed.

name: PolySkill: Learning Generalizable Skills Through Polymorphic Abstraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Reported evaluations include seen and unseen websites and Mind2Web.
summary: Introduces PolySkill, which separates a web-agent skill's goal from its execution so agents can learn and reuse skills across websites.

name: WEBSERV: A Full-Stack and RL-Ready Web Environment for Training Web Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebServ combines copy-on-write container environments with a compact DOM-derived browser interface for training web agents. Network-aware waiting supports action execution in single-page applications, with evaluations and reinforcement-learning experiments on WebArena-Lite.

name: Branch-and-Browse: Efficient and Controllable Web Exploration with Tree-Structured Reasoning and Action Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its reported task success and execution time results are from WebArena.
summary: Branch-and-Browse is a web agent framework that uses tree-structured subtasks, web state replay, and page action memory to explore and complete tasks.

name: WebATLAS: An LLM Agent with Experience-Driven Memory and Action Simulation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported success rate is measured on WebArena-Lite.
summary: WebATLAS is a web agent that stores interaction outcomes and simulates candidate actions before acting, using past experience to plan navigation on unseen websites.

name: SynthAgent: Adapting Web Agents with Synthetic Supervision
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces SynthAgent, which generates tasks by exploring website elements and refines them when observations reveal conflicts. A later trajectory-refinement stage removes misaligned behavior before fine-tuning agents for the target websites.

name: WebVIA: A Web-based Vision-Language Agentic Framework for Interactive and Verifiable UI-to-Code Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its main objective is UI code generation; the agent explores interface states to support that process.
summary: WebVIA combines a web UI exploration agent, interactive UI-to-Code generation, and validation of generated code's interactivity.

name: AgentPRM: Process Reward Models for LLM Agents via Step-Wise Promise and Progress
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The method addresses agent tasks broadly, with web shopping and browser navigation named as examples.
summary: AgentPRM scores sequential agent decisions by their promise and progress toward a goal, with web shopping and browser navigation among the motivating tasks.

name: WebCoach: Self-Evolving Web Agents with Cross-Session Memory Guidance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebCoach, which condenses navigation logs into persistent episodic memory and retrieves experiences by similarity and recency. Runtime hooks selectively supply advice to browser agents, evaluated on WebVoyager without retraining the underlying models.

name: Can We Stop Malicious AI? KILLBENCH: A Benchmark for External AI Kill Switch Feasibility
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5).
summary: KillBench evaluates external prompt-style signals intended to halt maliciously operating web agents, across harmful scenarios and agent configurations.

name: Building Browser Agents: Architecture, Security, and Practical Solutions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Broader claims about the safety of general-purpose browsing are the paper's position, not a catalog conclusion.
summary: Reports architectural and security lessons from building a browser agent, including hybrid accessibility-tree and visual context, browser tooling and programmatic constraints. A WebGames evaluation accompanies the discussion of reliability and specialization.

name: Fara-7B: An Efficient Agentic Model for Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces FaraGen synthetic web trajectories, a compact screenshot-based action model, and WebTailBench for underrepresented browser tasks.

name: BrowseSafe: Understanding and Preventing Prompt Injection Within AI Browser Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: BrowseSafe builds a benchmark of prompt injections in realistic HTML for browser agents and evaluates defenses against attacks that can affect agent actions.

name: Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports only preliminary generalization to unseen tasks in similar environments.
summary: PRAXIS stores action outcomes and retrieves past state-action-result examples to guide agent decisions, with evaluation on the REAL web browsing benchmark.

name: MCP vs RAG vs NLWeb vs HTML: A Comparison of the Effectiveness and Efficiency of Different Agent Interfaces to the Web (Technical Report)
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison uses four simulated e-shops.
summary: Compares HTML browsing, RAG, MCP, and NLWeb interfaces for web agents performing product search, comparison, and checkout tasks in four simulated e-shops.

name: LegalWebAgent: Empowering Access to Justice via LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LegalWebAgent separates user-needs clarification, webpage browsing, and actions such as form completion or scheduling. A 15-task evaluation studies legal-service workflows relevant to Québec civil-law users, using HTML and screenshot observations.

name: Privacy Practices of Browser Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract describes artifact release as planned; the annotation does not independently verify availability.
summary: Presents a privacy evaluation framework for browser agents covering component weaknesses, website defenses, tracking, privacy-related prompts and personal-data leakage. The framework is applied to deployed browser-agent tools.

name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.

name: WebOperator: Action-Aware Tree Search for Autonomous Agents in Web Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports experiments on WebArena and WebVoyager.
summary: WebOperator uses tree search, action filtering, and path checks before replay to explore web tasks and backtrack while accounting for irreversible actions.

name: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: NestBrowse organizes browser actions in a nested framework that separates interaction control from page exploration. It evaluates this design for deep information seeking beyond snippet retrieval and direct URL fetching.

name: Permission Manifests for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Proposes agent-permissions.json, a website manifest for declaring which interactions web agents may perform, with optional references to APIs.

name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.

name: FronTalk: Benchmarking Front-End Development as Conversational Code Generation with Multi-Modal Feedback
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Its main task is front-end code generation; web agents explore generated sites to assess and critique implementations.
summary: FronTalk benchmarks multi-turn front-end code generation from text and visual feedback; a web agent explores generated sites for evaluation and in AceCoder.

name: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ColorBrowserAgent converts human feedback into reusable website knowledge and uses that knowledge to guide progressive context summaries. It evaluates the resulting memory and adaptation mechanisms on long browser workflows.

name: When Bots Take the Bait: Exposing and Mitigating the Emerging Social Engineering Attack in Web Automation Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies deceptive social-engineering web patterns targeting browser automation agents and proposes defenses against bait-based manipulation.

name: WebTrap Park: An Automated Platform for Systematic Security Evaluation of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces WebTrap Park, a platform that turns web-agent security risks into executable tasks and assesses concrete interactions with live pages. It compares agent frameworks without requiring modifications to their implementations.

name: ExpSeek: Self-Triggered Experience Seeking for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ExpSeek uses step-level entropy signals to decide when a web agent should request experience-based guidance. It supplies guidance tailored to the current step and evaluates the intervention across web-agent benchmarks.

name: MalURLBench: A Benchmark Evaluating Agents' Vulnerabilities When Processing Web URLs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: MalURLBench evaluates how LLM-based web agents handle disguised malicious URLs across attack scenarios; the paper also analyzes attack factors and proposes URLGuard.
