publication.title: WebArbiter: A Generative Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
publication.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

name: WebArbiter: A Principle-Guided Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebArbiter generates reasoned action-preference verdicts for web navigation, using reasoning distillation followed by reinforcement learning. It introduces WebPRMBench and evaluates both preference judgments and reward-guided trajectory search.

name: How do Visual Attributes Influence Web Agents? A Comprehensive Evaluation of User Interface Design Factors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces VAF, a controlled pipeline that varies webpage appearance while retaining item semantics. It measures both agent clicks and reasoning references to study which visual design factors change browsing decisions.

name: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DynaWeb learns a world model that predicts web-page representations after actions and uses it to generate policy-training rollouts. It interleaves these rollouts with expert trajectories and evaluates the trained web agents on WebArena and WebVoyager.

name: SimGym: Traffic-Grounded Browser Agents for Offline A/B Testing in E-Commerce
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported validation compares simulated results with human outcomes from UI changes on one major e-commerce platform.
summary: SimGym runs traffic-grounded synthetic buyers as browser agents to compare e-commerce storefront variants offline, using buyer profiles derived from production interactions.

name: Avenir-Web: Human-Experience-Imitating Multimodal Web Agents with Mixture of Grounding Experts
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Avenir-Web combines multiple grounding specialists with procedural experience, a task checklist and adaptive memory. It evaluates this planning and execution framework on live Online-Mind2Web tasks.

name: WebSentinel: Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebSentinel identifies suspicious webpage segments and checks each against its surrounding page context to detect and locate prompt injections. Its evaluation uses both contaminated and clean webpage datasets.

name: Do Web Agents Investigate Before They Decide?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MIRAGE, a web decision benchmark where agents must actively uncover evidence that can contradict the visible context. Separate investigation, reasoning, decision, and hallucination measures diagnose failures beyond reaching the right page.

name: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: MUZZLE evaluates web-agent exposure to indirect prompt injection by finding attack surfaces in agent trajectories and refining injected instructions from execution feedback.

name: ICA: Information-Aware Credit Assignment for Visually Grounded Long-Horizon Information-Seeking Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Information-Aware Credit Assignment scores intermediate information gathered by web agents, using rendered webpage snapshots to compare evidence across trajectories.

name: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CATTS allocates additional inference computation when an agent’s action votes show uncertainty. The paper compares voting and arbiter strategies and evaluates this selective scaling on WebArena-Lite, Online-Mind2Web and GoBrowse.

name: Scaling Web Agent Training through Automatic Data Generation and Fine-grained Evaluation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This work uses constraint-based progress evaluation to retain partially successful web trajectories for training. It introduces BookingArena for structured booking tasks and studies a distilled agent trained with the resulting data.

name: SPILLage: Agentic Oversharing on the Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Formalizes and measures natural agentic oversharing when browser agents handle private user emails and calendars across live websites.

name: OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OpAgent combines multi-task GUI fine-tuning with online web reinforcement learning using outcome judgments and rule-based progress rewards. A modular planner, grounder, reflector and summarizer support navigation and recovery, evaluated separately from the underlying trained policy.

name: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AutoWebWorld turns finite-state task models into interactive websites whose actions and goal states can be checked programmatically. It generates verified trajectories for training and evaluates transfer to WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web.

name: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Any Customized UI
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EmbeWebAgent embeds agent access into existing web applications through frontend observations and a page-specific function registry. Its workflow combines GUI primitives, composite actions and MCP tools, demonstrated in a live interface.

name: World-Model-Augmented Web Agents with Action Correction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: WAC has a web-agent action model consult a world model, simulate action outcomes and use judge feedback to correct actions before execution.

name: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents for Contextual Reasoning with User History
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Persona2Web tests whether web agents can resolve ambiguous requests using preferences implicit in a user’s history. Its reasoning-aware evaluation compares agent architectures and history-access strategies on personalized tasks on the open web.

name: Web Agents Should Use Typed Actions Instead of Click-Based Browsing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Proposes web verbs as typed actions for web agents, exposing operations with structured inputs, outputs and conditions so agents can compose auditable workflows.

name: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CowCorpus records interleaved human and agent actions during web navigation and identifies distinct patterns of user intervention. Models trained to anticipate these interventions are integrated into live web agents and assessed in a user study.

name: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic Web Agents via State Machine Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: ActionEngine explores web applications to build an updateable state-machine memory of GUI states, operations and transitions. It generates complete task programs from that memory, using reactive repair to handle changed interfaces or missing knowledge.

name: Atomicity for Agents: Exposing, Exploiting, and Mitigating TOCTOU Vulnerabilities in Browser-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Identifies time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race vulnerabilities when web pages mutate between agent planning and action execution.

name: TimeWarp: Evaluating Web Agents by Revisiting the Past
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: TimeWarp tests web agents across multiple versions of the same sites, varying visual design, frontend code and workflows. TimeTraj transfers plans across versions to collect training trajectories and study robustness to interface change.

name: WebFactory: Automated Compression of Foundational Language Intelligence into Grounded Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebFactory, a GUI-agent training pipeline that synthesizes websites, generates tasks and trajectories, and trains with decomposed rewards. Offline and online transfer evaluations examine agents trained on the generated environments.

name: STRUCTUREDAGENT: Planning with AND/OR Trees for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces STRUCTUREDAGENT, a web-agent planning framework that interleaves execution with dynamic AND/OR trees, supporting node repair and exploration of alternative plans.

name: Enhancing Web Agents with a Hierarchical Memory Tree
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Hierarchical Memory Tree (HMT), which organizes web-agent trajectories by intent, stage and action, then uses the hierarchy to plan and act on websites.

name: Why Do LLM-based Web Agents Fail? A Hierarchical Planning Perspective
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Presents a hierarchical planning framework for evaluating web agents at planning, execution and replanning stages, and reports low-level execution as the main failure source.

name: ClawTrap: A MITM-Based Red-Teaming Framework for Real-World OpenClaw Security Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents a man-in-the-middle network red-teaming framework for evaluating autonomous OpenClaw agents under live traffic manipulation.

name: ContractSkill: Repairable Contract-Based Skills for Multimodal Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract limits its portability evidence to transfer within a benchmark family, not generalization across arbitrary benchmarks.
summary: Turns draft web-agent skills into structured executable artifacts that support deterministic checks, fault localization and local repair. VisualWebArena and MiniWoB experiments examine execution and reuse within the same benchmark family.

name: Ego2Web: A Web Agent Benchmark Grounded in Egocentric Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Ego2Web pairs first-person videos with online tasks that require agents to connect the user’s physical context to web actions. It also evaluates an automatic task judge against human judgments and analyzes failures in video understanding and web execution.

name: IntentWeave: A Progressive Entry Ladder for Multi-Surface Browser Agents in Cloud Portals
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The prototype and user study are set on a single cloud website.
summary: Introduces IntentWeave, a design space and browser-extension prototype for placing web-agent assistance across browser surfaces, evaluated through a study of three entry strategies.

name: The Cognitive Firewall:Securing Browser Based AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Via Hybrid Edge Cloud Defense
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes a split-compute browser defense pairing a local visual sentinel, a cloud planner, and deterministic policy enforcement against indirect prompt injection.

name: WebTestBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents towards End-to-End Automated Web Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebTestBench for end-to-end website testing, separating checklist generation from defect detection. Its WebTester baseline evaluates test coverage, detection and sustained interaction across web application categories.

name: Emergence WebVoyager: Toward Consistent and Transparent Evaluation of (Web) Agents in The Wild
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Audits sources of ambiguity and operational variation in WebVoyager evaluation and introduces standardized guidance for task setup, failure handling, annotation and reporting. Emergence WebVoyager applies this protocol to a web-agent evaluation.

name: When Users Change Their Mind: Evaluating Interruptible Agents in Long-Horizon Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Interruptions are evaluated through synthesized scenarios in a simulation framework.
summary: Introduces InterruptBench, a WebArena-Lite-derived benchmark that tests how long-horizon web-navigation agents handle mid-task user additions, revisions, and retractions.

name: Read More, Think More: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Studies HTML and accessibility-tree observations for web agents, relating their usefulness to model capability and thinking budget, and proposes diff-based observation history to save tokens.

name: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies persistent web-agent memory contamination introduced through environmental observations instead of direct memory access. Experiments on WebArena and VisualWebArena examine cross-session effects and how interaction failures alter susceptibility.

name: The Tool Illusion: Rethinking Tool Use in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Presents a controlled study of higher-level tool use in web agents across tool sources, backbone models, frameworks, and evaluation benchmarks.

name: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebSP-Eval evaluates agents carrying out website security and privacy tasks such as preference changes and session management. A browser extension controls account and initial state across runs, enabling analysis of failures on stateful UI controls.

name: Structured Distillation of Web Agent Capabilities Enables Generalization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported training uses one teacher model and trajectories from six web environments.
summary: Introduces Agent-as-Annotators, which uses modular LLM roles to synthesize and filter web-agent trajectories for supervised training of a smaller web agent.

name: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract states that artifacts will be released; this annotation does not independently verify release status or licenses.
summary: Presents MolmoWebMix, combining synthetic browser trajectories, human demonstrations and GUI perception data, and MolmoWeb screenshot-to-action policies trained from it. Browser benchmarks also test parallel rollouts with best-of-N selection.

name: ClawBench: Can AI Agents Complete Everyday Online Tasks?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces ClawBench, 153 everyday tasks on production websites in 15 categories; an interception layer blocks each final submission so bookings, purchases and job applications are scored without side effects.

name: WebForge: Breaking the Realism-Reproducibility-Scalability Trilemma in Browser Agent Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents WebForge, a pipeline that plans, generates, refines and validates self-contained interactive websites. WebForge-Bench uses these environments to evaluate browser agents across domains and controlled difficulty levels.

name: From Imitation to Discrimination: Progressive Curriculum Learning for Robust Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported evaluation is on Mind2Web.
summary: Introduces the Triton dataset and a staged training curriculum for text-based web navigation agents, using hard-negative HTML examples to train element discrimination and longer task execution.

name: WebXSkill: Skill Learning for Autonomous Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebXSkill pairs parameterized action programs with step-level language guidance, mining reusable skills from synthetic browser-agent traces. A URL-based graph supports retrieval, and deployment alternates between direct program execution and guided native planning.

name: RiskWebWorld: A Realistic Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces RiskWebWorld, an interactive benchmark of e-commerce risk-management tasks for GUI agents on websites, with Gymnasium infrastructure for evaluation and agentic RL.

name: StressWeb: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Web Agent Robustness under Realistic Interaction Variability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The tests use constructed, controllable web environments with clean workflows as baselines.
summary: Introduces a web-agent stress-testing benchmark with controlled changes to layouts, interaction semantics, and execution for diagnosing behavior under varied conditions.

name: WebUncertainty: Dual-Level Uncertainty Driven Planning and Reasoning For Autonomous Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebUncertainty adapts planning mode to task uncertainty and guides action-level tree search with confidence-derived uncertainty estimates. Its evaluations examine autonomous execution of dynamic, long-horizon web tasks on WebArena and WebVoyager.

name: Mango: Multi-Agent Web Navigation via Global-View Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports experiments on WebVoyager and WebWalkerQA.
summary: Proposes Mango, a multi-agent web-navigation method that selects starting URLs using Thompson Sampling and stores navigation history to inform later attempts.

name: PageGuide: Browser extension to assist users in navigating a webpage and locating information
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). PageGuide assists users with navigation and verification; the abstract reports a user study.
summary: PageGuide is a browser extension that highlights evidence for answers on a page and guides users through web pages with evidence captured at each step.

name: AutoSurfer -- Teaching Web Agents through Comprehensive Surfing, Learning, and Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AutoSurfer explores website actions breadth-first, retaining page and trajectory knowledge to guide task synthesis and trajectory refinement. It evaluates the resulting training data by fine-tuning a web agent on WebArena and examining synthesized-task diversity.

name: cotomi Act: Learning to Automate Work by Watching You
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported task score uses the 179-task WebArena human-evaluation subset.
summary: cotomi Act is a browser agent that executes multi-step tasks and turns observed user browsing into persistent knowledge shared with users.

name: WAAA! Web Adversaries Against Agentic Browsers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates agentic browsers against classical web attacks and visual social-engineering lures beyond indirect prompt injection.

name: Region4Web: Rethinking Observation Space Granularity for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Reorganizes webpage accessibility trees into functional regions through hierarchical decomposition and semantic abstraction. PageDigest supplies a persistent region-level observation to web agents, evaluated on WebArena.

name: WebTrap: Stealthy Mid-Task Hijacking of Browser Agents During Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports experiments on browser-agent tasks based on extended WASP and InjecAgent environments.
summary: WebTrap injects mid-task instructions into browser-agent navigation to steer an agent toward an attacker goal before it resumes the user's task.

name: SimPersona: Learning Discrete Buyer Personas from Raw Clickstreams for Grounded E-Commerce Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported evaluation covers held-out live storefronts and buyer behavior.
summary: SimPersona learns buyer types from clickstreams and uses persona tokens to condition web agents trained on browsing traces for live storefront tasks.

name: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported identification results come from four web environments.
summary: A study shows that websites can infer the model behind a browser agent from passively recorded UI actions and timing traces across web tasks.

name: SaaS-Bench: Can Computer-Use Agents Leverage Real-World SaaS to Solve Professional Workflows?
notes: The complete retained official abstract and cached official README were reviewed.
summary: SaaS-Bench evaluates browser agents on professional workflows across self-hosted applications. Weighted checkpoints measure task completion and partial progress, with application-state checks and configured content judges documented in the official harness.

name: PersonaFingerprint: Measuring Persona Inference on Modern Websites with LLM-Driven Browsing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The computer-use agent serves as browsing infrastructure for a privacy study.
summary: PersonaFingerprint studies persona inference from encrypted web traffic, using a persona-constrained computer-use agent to browse real websites and collect traces.

name: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its agent evaluation uses generated tasks in sandbox shops.
summary: ShopGym builds sandbox e-commerce storefronts from live shops and generates catalog-grounded tasks for evaluating web shopping agents in resettable environments.

name: Skim: Speculative Execution for Fast and Efficient Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its approach uses predictable patterns across queries of the same type on a site.
summary: Introduces Skim, a speculative execution framework for web agents that learns site URL and answer patterns offline, then uses them to answer matching queries with a small model.

name: DocOS: Towards Proactive Document-Guided Actions in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DocOS benchmarks agents that search online documentation and translate procedural instructions into GUI actions in interactive web environments. It separates failures to retrieve useful procedures from failures to ground retrieved instructions into executable actions.

name: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Weasel selects web-agent training steps by balancing importance and diversity across states, sites and interaction patterns. It also prunes training accessibility trees around known action targets and regenerates rationales to match the model’s reasoning style.

name: Agent JIT Compilation for Latency-Optimizing Web Agent Planning and Scheduling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Agent JIT compilation turns browser task descriptions into validated executable plans containing model calls, tools and parallel work. A cost-based scheduler and pre/postcondition protocol target latency and incorrect tool use in web-agent execution.

name: DRIVE: Modeling Skills at the Reasoning and Interaction Levels for Web Agents under Continual Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: DRIVE separates reusable reasoning skills from page-specific interaction skills for web agents, retrieving both to plan tasks and execute actions on websites.

name: PANDO: Efficient Multimodal AI Agents via Online Skill Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Analyzes inefficiency in VisualWebArena trajectories and distills reusable online skills to reduce repeated actions and token overhead in multimodal web agents.

name: PRO-CUA: Process-Reward Optimization for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: PRO-CUA trains computer-use agents with step-level RL, scoring candidate actions from live rollouts with a process reward model and evaluating on live web benchmarks.

name: GTA: Generating Long-Horizon Tasks for Web Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GTA generates multi-hop web-agent tasks and executable trajectories through crawling, retrieval, and validation, releasing a benchmark built from over 50 websites.

name: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents: Comprehensive Evaluation with a Lightweight Framework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a lightweight framework for evaluating HTML reduction in web agents, using Minimal Failure Set coverage to assess pruning and optimize latency.

name: Learning to Adapt: Self-Improving Web Agent via Cognitive-Aware Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SCALE, which uses exploration roles and graph planning to train web agents, and SCALE-20k, a dataset of tasks and demonstrations from real websites.

name: Masking Stale Observations Helps Search Agents -- Until It Doesn't: A Regime Map and Its Mechanism
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Studies when masking older retrieved pages helps long-horizon search agents manage context, using offline and live-web search benchmarks and analysis of reopened pages.

name: OpenWebRL: Demystifying Online Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning for Visual Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports results on Online-Mind2Web and DeepShop.
summary: Introduces OpenWebRL, a framework for training visual web agents with online multi-turn reinforcement learning on live websites, including browser infrastructure and success judging.

name: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval extracts reusable sub-procedures from completed web trajectories and represents them as paired text and code. Skills are retrieved against both the current webpage state and the task goal at intermediate execution steps.

name: AsyncWebRL: Efficient Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Step Visual Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AsyncWebRL overlaps web-agent rollouts, updates and policy refresh while managing screenshot handling and a persistent rollout pool. It also replaces trajectory-length normalization in multi-step GRPO to reduce verbose failed trajectories, with throughput and out-of-distribution evaluation.

name: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SUPERBROWSER combines screenshot-based target proposals with separate orchestration, planning and action roles. A bounded ledger and context-eviction process retain recent actions, task facts and checkpoints during browser execution.

name: AliyunConsoleAgent: Training Web Agents in Real-World Cloud Environments via Distillation and Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AliyunConsoleAgent trains browser agents to verify documented procedures against changing cloud-console UIs through trajectory distillation and online GRPO. Provisioned rollout environments and backend audit-log checks support training and outcome evaluation.

name: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebChallenger builds a hierarchical DOM-derived page representation for selective observation, reusable site maps and compound actions. The framework combines these mechanisms without model fine-tuning and evaluates generalization across multiple web-agent benchmarks.

name: MemVenom: Triggered Poisoning of Multimodal Memories in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports tests across multiple web-agent frameworks and vision-language models.
summary: Introduces MemVenom, a black-box attack that plants coordinated text and image content in web-agent memory to trigger retrieval and redirect later actions.

name: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: StakeBench evaluates prompt-injection harm to different stakeholders in shopping web-agent workflows. Its executable cases separate attack objectives and assess both outcomes and execution processes to reveal how the same attack pattern can affect different parties.

name: Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The evaluation injects seven deceptive patterns into existing web environments.
summary: Introduces WebDecept, a plugin for injecting deceptive e-commerce interface patterns during web-agent tasks and evaluating how multimodal agents respond.

name: Running the Gauntlet: Hard Agentic Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). The benchmark uses five controlled web-based professional applications.
summary: Introduces GauntletBench, a web-based benchmark of vision-intensive tasks in five professional applications for assessing agent perception, 3D reasoning, and generalisation.

name: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its state tracking relies on websites exposing a deterministic semantic MDP.
summary: Introduces WebStep, a web-agent benchmark that records semantic states behind GUI interactions to analyze exploration, execution accuracy, and decisive errors across task steps.

name: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SkillMigrator, a web agent that turns successful interactions into reusable skills and transfers them between sites by matching page layouts and live element references.

name: When Web Agents Finish but Still Fail: Reproducible Triggers and Trace Diagnostics for Parallel Web Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark concerns parallel web exploration and answer synthesis.
summary: Introduces Parallel WebBench for parallel web exploration and uses verified URL trajectories to diagnose search loops, incomplete answers, and failures after evidence retrieval.

name: Fara-1.5: Scalable Learning Environments for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds browser-agent training trajectories with live and synthetic environments, solvers, user simulation, and complementary correctness and efficiency verifiers.

name: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PEEU explores web environments and turns hindsight experience into aligned high-level planning supervision. A hierarchical task-decomposition analysis examines why atomic-skill competence alone does not ensure planning generalization across websites.

name: Ko-WideSearch: A Korean Breadth-Search Benchmark for Exhaustive Set Enumeration by Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its tasks assess exhaustive web search and table answers.
summary: Introduces Ko-WideSearch, a Korean web-agent benchmark that asks agents to find every member of a set and fill a table of attributes for each member.

name: BaRA: Budget-constrained and Reliable Web Data Collection Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its focus is site-level data collection within an interaction budget.
summary: Introduces BaRA, a web data-collection agent that discovers live site links, checks extracted text, images, and videos, and uses history to recover from failures.

name: Untrusted Content Masking for Web Agents with Security Guarantees
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Untrusted Content Masking uses DOM structure to redact untrusted webpage regions before agent observation. A sandboxed interaction interface separates privileges so browser actions can proceed under the proposed trust-boundary model without exposing protected content to the planner.

name: WebRetriever: A Large-Scale Comprehensive Benchmark for Efficient Web Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebRetriever evaluates navigation, knowledge-assisted interaction and end-to-end information-extraction workflows under separate protocols. Its NavEval judge uses richer interaction context to diagnose cases where navigation success does not translate into useful task completion.

name: Prismata: Confining Cross-Site Prompt Injection in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Prismata, a defense for web agents that assigns trust labels to page content and enforces them by redacting content and restricting agent actions.

name: Designing Agent-Ready Websites for AI Web Agents: A Framework for Machine Readability, Actionability, and Decision Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison uses two versions of one website prototype in a controlled experiment.
summary: Proposes an agent-ready website design framework for e-commerce browser agents and compares it with a human-oriented site on shopping tasks, outcomes, steps, and token use.

name: Broken Gates: Re-evaluating Web Bot Defenses in the Age of LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Measures how autonomous LLM browser agents interact with commercial bot-management and anti-automation defenses on the web.

name: PersonaTrail: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents through Browsing Trails
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces PersonaTrail, a benchmark for personalized web agents using browsing histories, and PACMem, a structured memory method for guiding navigation.

name: From Monoliths to Swarms: A Study of Attack Surface Evolution in the Transition to Multi-Agent Web Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Categorizes structural attack surfaces that emerge when single-agent browser systems are decomposed into multi-agent web workflows.

name: StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported attack results depend on agents following a chain of referenced pages.
summary: Introduces StepJack, a benchmark of indirect prompt injections that split an adversarial goal across pages on a computer-use agent's web navigation path.

name: WebRider: Persona-Conditioned Intent Controllers for Live-Web Assistance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). RiderBench evaluates live-web contracts across 42 public websites.
summary: Introduces WebRider, a live-web agent that maintains intent contracts while carrying out guarded browser actions, and RiderBench for auditing those contracts across websites.

name: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Site Browser Agents with Complex Actions and Perception
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: CAP builds cross-site browser workflows by decomposing websites into operation and perception requirements and recomposing them into tasks. Its judge-based evaluation diagnoses complex interactions and visual-perception failures across real websites.

name: Navigation Alone Is Not Enough: Evaluating Explanatory Assistive UI Agents
notes: Packaged tasks use recorded linear transition graphs. Reported model experiments use a text-input validation subset, so their results are not evidence of screenshot-based navigation performance. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3.3 Interface states and task annotations; 3.4 Evaluation; 4.1 Models and experimental setup; 5 Discussion).
summary: Introduces NeXUI, an assistive UI-agent benchmark that evaluates navigation together with interface-grounded explanations and user oversight in recorded interface states.

name: SkillLens: Visual Skill Cards for Retrieval-Augmented GUI Action Prediction and On-Policy Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported student comparison uses 119 tasks from ten websites absent from training.
summary: Introduces SkillLens visual skill cards for retrieved GUI action guidance and CardDistill for training an action-prediction student that runs without retrieval on website tasks.

name: SynWeaver: Website-Prior Task and Trajectory Co-Synthesis for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SynWeaver explores a website to build a map of page states and executable interactions, then learns website priors for task proposals. Joint task/trajectory synthesis revises inconsistent pairs and verifies or repairs the resulting supervision.

name: Wuying-Browser-Agent: Real-World Centric Fundamental Long-Horizon Browser Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines a browser execution framework, recovery-oriented supervision, and online reinforcement learning, with a bilingual live-web task benchmark.

name: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces BrowserForge, which combines broad website sourcing, parallel browser sandboxes, and task-proposer/solver interaction to collect verified web trajectories. The pipeline uses page structure during synthesis but trains a policy that acts from screenshots.

name: From Blind Edits to Verified Repair: Building Trustworthy User-Side LLM Agents for Web Accessibility
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds a local browser-extension agent that generates and verifies additive CSS repairs for WCAG web accessibility violations.

name: Learning Simple Test-Time Environments for LLM Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Test-Time Environment Decomposition, which uses trial interaction to break complex web observations into simpler modules. A label-free adaptation procedure learns from these sub-environments and studies whether their gains compose in full web tasks.

name: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.

name: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes an online teaching framework that decides which web-agent episodes warrant a stronger teacher and which trajectory turns merit training. A solvability gate and score-guided trimming aim to preserve first-attempt performance while reducing teaching and training costs.

name: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OdoBot builds a model of web-application behavior from successful task demonstrations and uses it to guide task execution. Its Canvas LMS evaluation compares token use and completion with existing web agents.

name: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AutoTailor compiles web trajectories into reusable browser-automation APIs, then filters and dynamically revises the capability inventory. WebArena experiments distinguish API-only operation from an agent that can fall back to ordinary reasoning and browser actions.

name: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The web investigations use corresponding local web environments.
summary: Introduces RiskChainBench, pairing obfuscated-message restoration with web-agent investigation of linked sites in labeled local web environments.

name: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported attack and task outcomes come from a 24-scenario benchmark.
summary: Presents the Verifiable Action Card (VAC), a browser approval mechanism that derives confirmations from pending actions and binds user approval to execution.

name: EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: EconSkills converts verified economic-data browsing traces into parameterized procedures with navigation, verification and recovery guidance. Its evaluation separates known-skill transfer from library retrieval, exposing the limits of approximate matches to new tasks.

name: Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains HTML-element relevance filters on Mind2Web trajectories and transfers them to WebArena to reduce irrelevant browser context. It also evaluates a zero-shot ColBERT retriever and documents baseline web-agent failure modes.

name: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: KNOWS benchmarks browser workflows that retrieve and synthesize information into documents, presentations and spreadsheets. Task-specific evaluators combine deterministic checks with model judgments, distinguishing partial progress from usable end-to-end artifact completion.

name: From Trajectories to Grounded Preferences: Process Preference Synthesis via Interaction Element Graphs for Web PRMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SURFPRM, which turns web demonstrations into an interaction-element graph for synthesizing grounded negative actions. Its contrastive preference data trains process reward models to distinguish plausible on-page alternatives and guide downstream trajectory search.

name: Learning from Others, Acting for You: Cross-User Memory Sharing for LLM Agents
notes: Main Mind2Web evaluation uses 252 recorded tasks assigned to 20 simulated users, frozen demonstration-derived memory and task-macro step metrics; it is not a live-browser completion test. The main split withholds same-site local experience, and sharing gains shrink when local coverage rises. Mind2Web has no preference channel; preference claims come from separate service and coding settings. User-bound retrieval is not a demonstrated privacy or security guarantee.
summary: ShareMem consolidates reusable experience across users while keeping preference retrieval user-bound; its web evaluation predicts target elements and actions on recorded Mind2Web states.

name: ORBIT: A Framework for Multi-Agent Safety and Security Evaluations
notes: BrowserART uses an accessibility-tree action interface, while the desktop adapter uses mouse, keyboard and screenshots. The adapted tasks are not claimed to preserve the constructs of their source benchmarks. Experiments cover a representative configuration slice with fixed attack templates; the OS-Harm results are imported from prior work using a different model and stack. Browser defense tables also differ in baseline versus defended judges and in judged benign denominators. Human judge validation used one grader. These results do not establish a universally effective defense. The linked repository and its code/data licenses were not independently inspected, and no experiment was run.
summary: Inspect-based framework that varies multi-agent roles, communication, attacks and defenses, with BrowserGym and virtual-desktop GUI adapters alongside coding and other tool scenarios.

name: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Probe to Act, which lets browser agents request visual evidence linking DOM handles and screen regions before committing an operation. It retains selected interaction evidence as memory and studies both prompted use and distillation into open models.

name: Structured Interaction, Visual Localization, and Robust Execution for Complex Web Tasks: A Technical Report on the WebRetriever Challenge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes a WebRetriever agent that combines semantic webpage operations with visual localization when structured representations are insufficient. Hierarchical context management and fault-aware execution support processing tasks across concurrent browsers.

name: AdaptArena: Evaluating Test-Time Personalization of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AdaptArena to test whether web agents can infer unstated user preferences from relevant past trajectories and carry those preferences into new tasks. Its AdaptiveAgent baseline separates preference-retrieval challenges from failures in downstream web execution.

name: Action Conditioned Bisimulation For GUI Agent Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Defines a GUI-memory merge rule that treats two states as equivalent only when shared actions lead to matching outcomes and successor states. The training-free method replaces observation-similarity merging and is tested in closed-loop MiniWoB++ interaction.

name: How To Train Your World Model: Fine-tuning vs RAG for LM-based World Modeling
notes: Adjacent cross-domain study with WebShop as its web evaluation. WebShop uses text-rendered search/product pages and an explicit valid-action menu, not screenshot control or live purchases. A frozen policy proposes five actions; a world model predicts their next observations and the policy scores them before one is executed in the simulator. Utility is normalized environment reward, while fidelity uses a model judge; neither is a universal GUI task-success rate. Fine-tuning and retrieval use collected training experience; the hybrid masks same-episode retrieval, which does not establish general contamination freedom. The retained Atom and v1 HTML abstract wording differs; original bibliographic metadata and its abstract digest are preserved.
summary: Compares fine-tuned, retrieval-based and hybrid language-model world models for next-observation prediction and action selection in text environments including WebShop.

name: WebUIProof: Benchmarking WebUI Code Generators with UI-Agent Execution Harness
notes: Adjacent evaluation infrastructure: the target is generated WebUI functionality, not a general score for computer-use agents. This annotation is based on the complete retained abstract.
summary: Introduces an execution-based benchmark for generated web interfaces, with a headless-browser UI-agent harness that checks DOM interactions and functional assertions.

name: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes WebFovea, a vision-based live-web agent whose execution loop checks action parsing, browser effects, feedback accuracy, and observation delivery. The report analyzes failures such as coordinate mismatches and silent control interactions and documents corresponding harness changes.

name: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Models are evaluated with provider-native search or a shared retrieval harness.
summary: Introduces HyperBrowseComp, a multilingual benchmark for browsing agents that must connect evidence across open-web sources, including videos, scans, images, and maps.

name: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CLIFT, which certifies agent-generated verification signals against training-time judges and reuses them for per-step rewards and trajectory selection. At inference, a frozen question bank helps compare candidate web rollouts without querying an external judge.

name: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes Secure-CUA, which commits to per-action transactions before reading untrusted page content and separates content queries from GUI target selection. The paper formalizes its protection assumptions and evaluates benign task utility on WebArena.

name: Can LLMs Fix It Without Code? Toward Automated Verification of No-Code Bug Fixes
notes: The evaluation reuses 322 fixes from 12 generation configurations and is restricted to nine of 51 candidate issues after environment setup and sanity checks. Resolution counts any success in three runs with a 20-step episode limit; executor harnesses and decoding settings differ. Opening the update page triggers a harness-controlled switch to the fixed browser build. Checker behavior, reconstructed starting states and the two-author human reference limit interpretation. The replication package was linked by the paper but was not inspected.
summary: Tests natural-language no-code fixes through GUI execution in Linux Brave. Scripted fixed/buggy-state gates and issue-specific checkers distinguish fix outcomes from the executor's completion claims.

name: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Web$hell, an interface that compiles live pages into persistent information and action objects so agents can gather evidence, navigate websites, and reuse acquired content through shared operations.

name: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents MASTIF, a framework for comparing combinations of agent models, protocols, and implementation frameworks on web tasks, with an initial assessment using 300 Mind2Web tasks.

name: HyWe: Unifying Search and Operation for Real-World Hybrid Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces HyWe, which switches between information search and browser operation within one trajectory, alongside a demonstration pipeline and a benchmark of hybrid web tasks.

name: Glasseek: A Transparent Recipe for Training and Trustworthy Evaluation of DeepSearch Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Glasseek, a framework for deep-search agents that explore the open web, with trajectory construction, training across context compression, and a test-set leakage audit.

name: BrowseSafe++: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detection Across Web Contexts, Languages, and Browser Views
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Extends BrowseSafe with paired attacked and clean webpages in several representations, and studies text and screenshot detectors plus feedback-adapted prompt injections.

name: Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops
notes: Adjacent diagnostic research across simulators, policies, tools, coding and an offline Mind2Web subset. Models choose among supplied admissible actions; they do not generate actions or execute a closed-loop browser policy in the reported evaluation. The paired probes measure selected visible facts, not complete understanding or internal causation. Pooled results are not a web-only leaderboard, and the paper reports coverage limits and label-sensitivity analyses. No benchmark release, code, data or weights were independently inspected.
summary: Pairs factual probes with next-action choices on frozen agent traces, including Mind2Web, to diagnose reading-decision gaps without closed-loop execution.

name: Teaching Agents in their Own Style: Blackbox Teacher Distillation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces WebKD, which repairs failed student web-agent trajectories with minimal teacher edits and trains on corrections that preserve the student's reasoning style.

name: Why Generate a Click? Plug-in Decision Heads for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Adds decision heads to a frozen vision-language generator for selecting web actions and targets, with a confidence gate that falls back to text generation.

name: Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks
notes: Reviewed the complete retained abstract and selected exact-v1 method, evaluation and analysis sections. Adapter-bank and router training use source demonstrations. Domain scouting accesses target training-task intents and answer-stripped reference procedures; version scouting is task-free. No target-time gradients does not mean no target task information.
summary: WebMix uses a scout-produced interface manual to route mixtures of source-trained LoRA adapters for web agents, adapting to target interfaces without target-time gradient updates.

name: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
notes: Evaluation instructs the model to simulate compromise and measures planner outputs and permission appearance. Utility uses plan matching and LLM-judged element suitability; no steps are executed in that assessment. Assumes an honest first party, trusted browser/harness and untampered instrumentation; multi-page and availability attacks are outside scope. Parallel latency reduction is an unimplemented estimate.
summary: Intact records webpage element provenance and capabilities, isolates planning per element, and uses a browser harness to constrain actions and request consent for third-party interactions.

name: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas
notes: Reviewed the complete retained abstract and selected exact-v1 construction, evaluation and limitations sections. Main interactions and satisfaction ratings use LLM-simulated personas; human annotators validate selected outputs. The harness observes page text, with screenshots only for auditing. Results are not evidence about real demographic populations or desktop agents.
summary: PersonaCUABench varies simulated user requests and clarification dialogue over fixed web tasks, comparing task completion with requirement handling and persona-agent satisfaction ratings.

name: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Results are reported on the study's site and page templates and web tasks.
summary: Proposes constrained reinforcement learning for web agents that weighs request costs, latency and failure risk across multi-step website tasks.

name: SPIDES: Information-Flow Control for Browser Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 threat-model, policy, evaluation and limitations sections. Guarantees assume correct labels/trusted origins and a trusted browser/harness mediating actions; evaluation uses idealized approvals. Origin-level reader sets can miss recipient distinctions within one origin.
summary: SPIDES propagates HTML integrity and confidentiality labels into agent context and mediates browser actions with information-flow policies and approval gates, evaluated in the labeled MicroNet ecosystem.

name: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The tasks seek unique factual answers from live web evidence.
summary: OpenDS-World benchmarks multi-step research on the live open Web, requiring agents to search, interact with browsers and combine evidence across sources.

name: SkillShift-Bench: Benchmarking Skill Learning under Environment Evolution for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The controlled shifts are simulated across three self-hosted web systems.
summary: Introduces SkillShift-Bench to evaluate how web agents reuse learned skills when task context, visual perception, or execution conditions change across web systems.

name: AgentProofBench: Benchmarking Reusable Verifiers for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The resource covers four web services; the reported execution analysis covers 22 task families.
summary: Introduces AgentProofBench, a benchmark linking tests of reusable web-agent verification rules to subsequent execution from saved web states.

name: Harness-Model Collaboration for Long-Horizon Continual Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces HaMo, a continual-learning framework for web agents that retrieves strategy cards from past workflows and updates model parameters to reuse them.

name: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The generated trajectories teach short interactions; MiniWebAgent adds a planner for full tasks.
summary: Introduces MiniWeb for skill-labeled browser tasks, MiniWebGen for generating training trajectories, and MiniWebAgent for composing learned skills into web workflows.

name: Right Click, Wrong Box: Grading GUI Grounding by What a Click Does
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Proposes grading GUI grounding clicks by their executed outcomes and audits box-based scores on live web applications and ScreenSpot-v2 screenshots.

name: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Reconstruction uses browser-observable material collected after initial setup and authorization.
summary: Introduces WebAnything, a framework that reconstructs reusable, resettable website environments from real URLs for web-agent training and evaluation.

name: AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Experiments span a counterfactual sandbox and replay of real websites.
summary: Introduces AgentHeal, a benchmark of whether web agents detect access barriers, find legitimate alternative sources, and preserve the user's original goal.

name: InterA11y: Interactive Web Accessibility Error Detection with LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The evaluation covers 197 expert-annotated cases from 54 real webpages.
summary: Introduces InterA11y, a web accessibility evaluation system that guides LLM agents with rubrics and tools for inspecting and operating pages.

name: DynaRev: Benchmarking Web Agents under Dynamic Goal Revision
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported evaluation uses five models.
summary: Introduces DynaRev, a benchmark of 181 web-agent tasks whose goals change during execution, with trajectory-based measures of correctness, responsiveness, and efficiency.

name: AgentShield: Fortifying Web Applications Against AI Agents and Agentic Browsers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract also describes an obstruction-driven attack and defensive prompt injection techniques.
summary: Evaluates agentic browsers against web anti-bot defenses and introduces AgentShield, a behavioral fingerprinting framework for distinguishing agents from people.

name: ANGLER: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking with an Adaptive Attacker for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported attacks are evaluated across eight VLM-based web agents.
summary: Introduces REEF, a website benchmark with state-based attack verification, and ANGLER, which adapts attack lures using outcomes from web-agent rollouts.

name: PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PatchScout, a multi-agent method for collecting thematic documents from the live web by deciding when to explore a new information region.

name: When 200 OK Is Not an Answer: Silent Fetch Failures in Agentic Web Content Acquisition
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Studies silent failures in web content fetched by static and rendered-browser clients, and evaluates checks for whether HTTP 200 pages contain usable content.

name: From Local Skills to Long-Horizon Web Tasks: Progressive Skill Exploration for LLM Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported experiments use WebArena, WebVoyager, and WebShop.
summary: Introduces SCOPE, a training method for long web-agent tasks that discovers local skills from rollouts, composes them into chains, and expands them using failure experience.

name: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The environments reconstruct real websites under deterministic control.
summary: Introduces WebHarbor, a suite of 153 executable website environments and 3,518 tasks for evaluating and training GUI web agents on interactive workflows.

name: Voluntary Servitude: Weaponized Safety Warning Mechanisms for Controlling AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported reduction in exposure under corroboration is against a non-adaptive attacker.
summary: Studies fabricated hazard warnings in reviews that steer agents’ choices without explicit commands, including transfer to browser agents, and tests a corroboration requirement.

name: fastbrowse
notes: Python package fastbrowse 0.5.23 by Agent Labs (Python 3.13+), with a CLI, an MCP server (fastbrowse-mcp) and a JavaScript SDK. The browser layer speaks CDP through cdp-use; snapshot.js, ported from jev-ultrafast, indexes each frame's controls, viewport text and a freshness fingerprint, including open shadow roots. Per the design document, Jev chooses the operation and target among indexed controls (with relevance pruning on dense pages), an LLM proposes start addresses, plans checkable requirements, reads page text, writes non-secret field text and composes the answer, and code enforces freshness and hit-tests before input, no automatic retry of mutations, authorization for submit, pay, delete or send, secret redaction and budgets; a run counts as complete only when every requirement is evidenced. Browsers are Browser Use Cloud by default, local Chrome, or an existing CDP endpoint including Electron windows. Jev is reached through TypeSafe, OpenRouter or the Vercel AI Gateway. Benchmark comparisons in the README are the publisher's. Root LICENSE is MIT, with a NOTICE file. Code was read, not run.

name: OpenJev
notes: Models and code for an open replacement of a hosted System One decision API. A Qwen3 or Qwen3.5 backbone without its vocabulary head scores each option with a pointer head, so one pass answers every question in a request; a local server exposes POST /v1/systemone. Browser steps arrive as page text, numbered elements and recent actions, and the model chooses an operation (click, type, DONE and others) and a target element. The repository holds the wev package (data conversion for Mind2Web, NNetNav and WebChain, training, calibration, export, serving), teacher-collection scripts, the OpenJev-Bench browser-lane client (2,346 frozen steps stored in the Hub dataset alanhuangya/OpenJev-Data), locked results and the paper source; the paper is a Zenodo deposit (doi 10.5281/zenodo.22941164) with no catalog record. The models also answer general decisions such as triage and routing. Results are publisher-reported, and live-website numbers use an LLM judge. Not a fork, not archived. Code was read, not run.
summary: Decision models at 1.7B, 4B and 8B that answer typed questions with calibrated probabilities in one pass; trained on browser-agent steps and general decision data, they pick a web agent's next operation and element.

name: OpenBUA
notes: Chrome Manifest V3 extension (manifest version 1.9.1) whose agent loop is built on the pi-agent-core and pi-ai packages. Its tools (src/agent/tools.ts) read a paginated inventory of interactive DOM controls including open shadow roots, inspect forms, click elements or screenshot-pixel coordinates (used for canvas editors such as Google Docs), type, scroll, switch and open tabs, upload files, post to social sites and send webmail; capture_tab_screenshot returns the visible-tab image to the model. Actions run as scripts injected with chrome.scripting that dispatch synthetic pointer and mouse events (src/agent/browser-bridge.ts); the manifest requests no debugger permission. Before showing its human CAPTCHA gate, the bridge makes up to two automatic rounds in which a vision model is asked to click inside detected challenge regions (src/agent/captcha-auto.ts). It acts in the user's logged-in sessions and keeps a memory store with optional parallel worker windows. The README ends with 'MIT', but the inspected tree has no license file. The agent was not run.

name: OpenBrowser
notes: Published on PyPI as openbrowser-ai. The CodeAgent (src/openbrowser/code_use/service.py) sends a compact serialized DOM state with element indices and, unless vision is turned off, a JPEG screenshot; the model replies with Python that the executor runs in a persistent namespace. The MCP server exposes a single execute_code tool over the same namespace, and a CLI daemon keeps a browser session alive between commands. The repository also holds a hosted-platform backend and frontend, and infra/training with SFT, online GRPO and diffusion-language-model RL code for FormFactory form filling; the README links the two related papers on ResearchGate, not arXiv. Token and latency comparisons with other browser tools are publisher-reported and were not reproduced. Code was read, not run.
summary: Python browser-automation framework whose CodeAgent shows a model indexed DOM state and an optional screenshot, then runs the Python it writes against Chrome DevTools Protocol helpers in a persistent namespace.

name: Browserable
notes: Inspected at commit a3af19a6 (27 August 2025). The README sets up a Docker Compose stack (UI server, tasks server, MongoDB, Redis and MinIO) in which the user supplies one LLM key (Gemini, OpenAI or Claude) and a Steel or Hyperbrowser key; tasks/services/browser.js also accepts Browserbase or the repository's own browser service, which launches Playwright Chromium. In tasks/agents/browserable.js the act-on-tab action calls simpleActionHelper, whose loop takes a plain page screenshot and the current chunk of DOM elements with XPaths, asks a planner for high-level steps (replanning after five steps), and asks a runner for a Playwright method, arguments and element number; the older DOM-only and vision act helpers are commented out at that call site. The repository also contains deep-research and generative agents. The README's 90.4% WebVoyager figure is publisher-reported and was not reproduced. The README names Stagehand among the open-source projects it builds on. No code was run.

name: DomA
notes: The README presents DomA as a browser agent from Stay Browser, and the LICENSE notice names Dom Actions; the commercial store build adds video download, a userscript manager and ad blocking on top of this core. The service worker implements browser_* tools (tabs, navigation, page content, element lists, click, text click, type, select, scroll, script execution, clipboard). browser_screenshot tags up to 150 visible interactive elements with data-som-idx and composites numbers and borders onto a clean viewport capture, grouping the overflow into areas A1 to A5; clicks fall back to CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent through chrome.debugger. With the Jev switch on, a high-confidence Jev decision can execute a click or type without sending the image to the LLM. Models are user-supplied OpenAI-compatible endpoints. An MCP bridge (stdio server plus a local daemon on ports 3846/3847) and a CLI let Cursor, Claude or OpenClaw drive the extension. Not a fork, not archived. Code was read, not run.

name: Surfer-H-CLI
notes: Archived on GitHub, and the README marks it deprecated in favour of H Company's hosted Models API and Agent API and the hai-agents clients. The loop keeps the last three screenshots by default for the navigation step, which chooses click_element, write_element, scroll, go_back, refresh, wait, restart or answer; click and write targets are named elements that a localizer model (Holo1 or the structured Holo1.5 path) turns into viewport coordinates for Selenium ActionChains. Models are reached through OpenAI-compatible endpoints: H Company's hosted API, a local vLLM server, or a SageMaker deployment; one script uses GPT-4.1 as validator. A FastAPI agent_server.py and a Next.js frontend stream runs to a browser UI. Root LICENSE is the BSD 3-Clause text with an H Company copyright and does not cover the Holo weights. Code was read, not run.

name: Odysseys
notes: Each task has a SHA-1 ID, a prompt, a starting URL, a difficulty level, a reference step count, numbered rubric items with requirement and verification text, and SimilarWeb category tags. The README runs tasks with the OSWorld runner (Chrome in an Ubuntu VM, 100-step budget) after converting them with convert_odysseys_to_osworld.py, whose OSWorld evaluator is a placeholder; scoring is done afterwards by run_full_trajectory_per_rubric.py, which asks an LLM judge (by default gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview, the model the README uses, or an OpenAI-compatible model) whether any step satisfies each rubric item. Reported metrics are the averaged rubric score, the perfect rate and trajectory efficiency. The README says the starting URL is always Google, but 70 of the 200 tasks in odysseys.json start at another site, and the converter opens each task's own URL. Tasks run on live websites, so results can drift. README results are paper figures and were not reproduced.
summary: 200 long-horizon web tasks drawn from real browsing sessions, run on the live Internet in Chrome through the OSWorld runner and scored per rubric item by an LLM judge over the trajectory's screenshots and actions.

name: Wanta
notes: Recorded as adjacent: Wanta is a general agent host whose local tools are files, shell, skills, knowledge and SaaS connectors (OpenConnector), and its only graphical executor is the integrated browser. The Electron main process owns a WebContentsView per task page, Playwright attaches through a custom CDP transport over webContents.debugger, and an authenticated loopback bridge serves seven OpenCode tools: browser_navigate, browser_read (title, URL, dialog state and a Playwright AI-mode ARIA snapshot with refs), browser_click and browser_type on refs or unique selectors, browser_scroll, browser_screenshot and browser_dialog. The user shares the page and completes logins and CAPTCHAs; in Default Access the agent is told to hand sensitive actions to the user, which the design document calls a behavioural policy rather than a system guarantee. External agents keep their own accounts; hosted models, connectors and team workspaces need an OOMOL account. Packages for macOS, Windows and Linux. Root LICENSE is Apache-2.0.
