name: Bops
notes: Electron app (desktop/) that starts a local Next.js server (app/, lib/server/) on port 3210; version 0.0.28 in package.json, matching release tag v0.0.28 at 92ec73d, and the inspected commit 62c7f98 is later. Bots' tasks run on Orgo cloud computers launched from the bops-base template that orgo/bops-base.mjs builds from vm/ (Codex, the screen MCP and per-screen Chrome helpers). By default lib/server/computer-task.ts runs each thread on OpenAI's Responses API computer tool: Orgo's API returns a screenshot of the bot's screen, and every click, double-click, drag, scroll, typing or key press the model asks for is executed as xdotool commands through Orgo's bash endpoint, with the result screen sent back; the same loop offers a page_script tool that runs a short Playwright script on the screen's Chrome over CDP, a Linux shell, web search, a password vault and app, data and CRM tools. With BOPS_COMPUTER_TOOL=0 threads use OpenAI's Agents API with Codex and vm/screen_mcp.py, which exposes one screen's screenshot and input actions over MCP. Tasks on the user's own Mac run in a bot-owned Chrome; with Full access they also get a shell and the user's apps through Cua Driver behind vm/mac-ui-mcp.mjs, which hides sensitive apps, sends input only in the background and blocks quitting, copying and pasting (lib/server/local.ts). Per the README, reading runs at once while sending, creating and paying wait for the user's approval, and any screen can be watched live and taken over. Self-hosting requires an Orgo account and two OpenAI API keys, with Honcho, Composio, treg, AgentMail, AgentPhone and TypeSafe recommended or optional; signing in with Orgo instead routes provider calls through Orgo's hosted Bops Cloud (cloud/). Licensed FSL-1.1-ALv2 (fair source; competing products and hosted services are excluded, and each version becomes Apache-2.0 two years after release); components/message-ui/ is adapted from MIT-licensed code. Not a fork, not archived. Code was read, not run.

name: Gemini Browser Agent
notes: The README calls the project a research experiment and scaffolding. websocket_agent.py is a local WebSocket server that calls gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025 through google-genai with the browser computer-use environment; widget/ is an unpacked Manifest V3 extension with a side panel where the user connects to the bridge and enters a goal. Each turn the extension captures the visible tab with chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab, the bridge converts the model's 0-1000 normalized coordinates to viewport pixels, and the extension carries out clicks, typing, key presses, hovering, scrolling and navigation by injecting functions (chrome.scripting.executeScript) that dispatch synthetic DOM events at document.elementFromPoint. Drag and drop is approximated with mousedown and mouseup events, unhandled model actions return an unimplemented warning, and the side panel sets a step limit (default 10). It needs a Gemini API key and acts in the user's own browser without a sandbox; the README points to the author's separate gemini-computer-use repository for sandboxed runs. The repository has no license file at the inspected commit. Code was read, not run.

name: Xiryn
notes: Next.js app run locally (version 0.4.1 in package.json; tag v0.4.1 points at b8016b5, and the inspected commit 489e9c4 is later). Each agent's workstation is a Docker container built from workstation/: Debian (trixie-slim) with Xvfb, xfwm4 and a panel, Chromium, x11vnc and noVNC, xdotool and scrot, a persistent home volume, and an inactivity watchdog. lib/agent/tools.ts defines the tool belt for the Vercel AI SDK streamText loop: shell and fs_* through docker exec; screen_capture and screen_share (scrot JPEG through xiryn-shot); pointer_click, pointer_move, pointer_drag, pointer_scroll, key_type and key_press (xdotool in lib/workstation.ts), each returning a fresh screenshot; request_takeover; vault_list, vault_fill, request_payment_approval and request_secret; memory_write and memory_forget; web_search and web_fetch through Firecrawl; and delegate for squads. Observation is plain screenshots of a 1280x800 display with pixel coordinates; there is no accessibility tree or element annotation. Before each step the runtime keeps only the two most recent screenshots in full (docs/architecture.md). The vault fills saved logins and cards into fields without the model seeing them, and cards only after the owner approves the payment. The user can watch and take over the desktop, and the agent hands over at logins, payments, one-time codes or CAPTCHAs, with a Telegram notice when paired. Models come from the owner's keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The README's comparison with hosted agents is the author's own. Root LICENSE is MIT; not a fork, not archived. Code was read, not run.
summary: Self-hosted personal agent app that gives each agent its own Docker Linux desktop with Chromium, operated through screenshots and xdotool clicks and keys, with live take-over, memory, a vault and Telegram control.

name: TimeWarp
notes: Code for the TimeWarp paper, which the README's citation lists as to appear in the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track. env/ holds Flask apps for Wiki and News and an adapted copy of WebShop for Shop (with WebShop's MIT license text), plus a homepage app; each loads one of six numbered UI themes styled after different eras (the Wiki app also registers a seventh 'modern' theme), and new themes can be added as folders. Site data is downloaded from the Hugging Face dataset sparklabutah/timewarp-env-data. src/browsergym/timewarp registers timewarp.1 to timewarp.231 with BrowserGym; its task file has 231 tasks: 70 Wiki-only, 64 Shop-only, 47 News-only and 50 spanning two or three sites. Agents answer in free text, which is normalized and checked by string_match, number_match and list_match verifiers (AND-combined per task); 2 tasks use only the LLM judge (GPT-5 by default, or a locally served Gemma model). scripts/ runs AgentLab studies per site and sweeps models and UI versions; collectTeacherTraj/ provides a modified AgentLab loop and agent that save teacher trajectories, llamafactory/ has full and LoRA fine-tuning configs for training on them, and the README points to GPT-5 traces on Hugging Face. scripts/annotation holds the verifier authoring and audit tooling, results/ has page-measurement and visual-information validation data, and proofs/ has Lean 4 proofs of the appendix theory. The README shows an MIT badge without a link, and the tree has no root license file. Not a fork, not archived; no release. Code was read, not run.

name: System1-Agents
notes: Adjacent because browser and desktop control are two of several shipped domains; the package (s1a) is equally aimed at games, ALFWorld, ticket routing and an injection-guard rail. On a decision turn the System 1 model answers typed choice questions while a chat model keeps planning, typed values and the final answer. The browser front runs a stock openJiuwen browser subagent (pinned ThinkFlowLab fork of agent-core) over @playwright/mcp; its in-page probe numbers the visible controls of the top document's light DOM, and the decision model chooses an element plus an operation head (CLICK, TYPE_TEXT, PRESS_ENTER, SELECT, scrolling). OmniJev instead receives a page screenshot. The desktop agent drives a Windows or macOS app window through the external Cua Driver over MCP, clicking accessibility elements bound to a window snapshot. Decision models are reached through TypeSafe, OpenRouter or served endpoints; Cua-S1 Nano runs in process from a pinned trycua/cua subdirectory. Speed and cost tables in the README are the publisher's single-episode comparisons. The browser files carry Huawei copyright notices with ThinkFlowLab modifications under Apache-2.0. Code was read, not run.

notes: Open-source code of the webagent.cloud hosted service, published by webagent-cloud. A FastAPI server (server.py, webagent/api.py) with a bundled React UI accepts a prompt and runs it with the engine set by ENGINE_PROVIDER: Browser Use by default, or Notte, whose agent is fixed to gemini-2.5-flash with at most 30 steps. The browser comes from BROWSER_PROVIDER: a local Playwright Chromium over CDP, Browserbase or Steel; at the reviewed commit the Steel provider's create_session takes a context argument that the caller does not pass. Models are reached through Browser Use's chat clients for OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, Google and Groq; other provider values fall back to the OpenAI client. After a run, workflow_builder_service.py asks an LLM to extract parameters from the prompt and template the recorded actions with their element XPaths; workflow_replay_service.py replays those steps with Playwright (navigation, search, XPath clicks and typing, scrolling, key presses, uploads, dropdowns) without a model and, when an action fails, hands that step to the AI engine for up to three attempts. Tasks, runs and results are kept in a local SQLite database; results can be text or JSON validated against a supplied JSON Schema, and a webhook can be called on completion. The README's n8n, Zapier and Make integrations and Stagehand engine are not in the tree. Root LICENSE is MIT; not a fork, not archived; no release. Code was read, not run.

name: Agent Skill Induction (ASI)
notes: Research code by Zora Zhiruo Wang and coauthors. The agent (asi/agent.py) observes BrowserGym pages through the flattened accessibility tree by default, with HTML and screenshot inputs as options, and acts through BrowserGym's action set. run_online.py alternates solving WebArena tasks, judging the trajectory with the autoeval LLM evaluator, inducing website-specific skill functions (asi/induce/induce_actions.py) and testing them before they are added; the README also runs AWM and vanilla baselines from the same script. The repository vendors a copy of BrowserGym packages (browsergym/, Apache-2.0 per their pyproject files) and expects self-hosted WebArena sites. The root LICENSE is CC BY-SA 4.0. No code was run and no result was reproduced.
summary: Official code for agent skill induction on WebArena: an LLM judge checks each trajectory, successful episodes become Python skill functions, and skills join the action space only after generated tests pass.

name: Webfuse
notes: Webfuse serves an existing website through a configurable proxy session and injects Extensions on the client side without changes to the site's code. Its Automation API, callable from an Extension, provides perception (DOM snapshot, Base64 screenshot of the page, accessibility tree, text selection) and actuation (click, type, scroll, select, key press, mouse move, text selection), targeting an element, CSS selector, point coordinate or Webfuse element ID across shadow DOM and iframes; the screenshot method is documented for Chromium-based browsers only. The Session MCP Server exposes the same tools, plus navigate and page info, to MCP clients authenticated with a Space automation key. tool.applyD2Snap() applies the DOM downsampling method of arXiv 2508.04412, whose second author, Nicholas Piël, is named on the about page as Webfuse's CEO and founder; the about page also says Webfuse grew out of the team's Surfly session technology. The pricing page lists Spark and Forge monthly plans metered in virtual minutes, a custom Foundry tier and a 14-day free trial. Pricing, compliance claims and reliability were not independently tested.
summary: Web augmentation proxy that serves a site inside the user's browser and lets AI agents read DOM, screenshot or accessibility-tree snapshots and click, type or scroll through an automation API and a session MCP server.

notes: Predicate Systems Inc. was formerly SentienceAPI; www.sentienceapi.com redirects to this site. It has three parts. notes: The annotation was reviewed against the publisher PDF and the Crossref deposit for its DOI. Experiments have not been independently reproduced. The method, In-Context Learning Guidance (ICLG), has GPT-5.1 solve tasks offline and appends only its reasoning fields, not its low-level actions, to the student prompt; the teacher is not called while the student runs. Evaluation serves the 130 MiniWoB++ tasks locally, caps each run at 5 minutes and 25 interaction steps, counts a score of at least 0.5 as solved, and reports single runs: seven of ten students improve and three lose one task. Retry and refined-prompt ablations cover three students. The paper names no code release or arXiv version.
summary: Training-free protocol that turns a teacher model's offline reasoning traces into prompt guidance for open-weight browser agents; on MiniWoB++ it lifts solved student-task pairs from 208 to 271 across ten students.

notes: The homepage targets payer-portal and EHR workflows and says every run executes in a VM with laptop-like fingerprints and human-like input, with queued concurrency, video replay, per-action screenshots and logs, and HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. name: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Model in GUI World
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2025 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2025 Poster. Experiments were not reproduced. The grounding model, AssistGUIGrounder (AGG), pairs a SAM-pretrained ViT image encoder and a transformer query encoder with a two-layer box decoder. The data engine loads Common Crawl pages from 118 domains in a browser such as Chrome, scrolls them with Page Down and reads element data through UI Automation; grounding training used 0.36M web images with 22M annotations after smoothing, plus 27K mobile screenshots from WidgetCaption and RICO. ScreenSpot grounding covers mobile, desktop and web screenshots; agent fine-tuning covers MiniWob, AITW and Mind2Web. The paper gives github.com/showlab/AssistGUIGround for code and data; that repository returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-19. No arXiv version was found.
summary: Trains a 0.4B SAM-initialized GUI grounding model on 0.5M auto-collected web screenshots with 35M element annotations, then links it to a Qwen-VL planner through a position token for MiniWob, AITW and Mind2Web.

name: Yutori
notes: Yutori was founded by Abhishek Das, Devi Parikh and Dhruv Batra and announced its seed round in March 2025. Navigator models are called through an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint: the caller sends a screenshot and a task, the model returns actions as tool calls, and the caller executes them and sends a fresh screenshot in an agent loop. n1.5 drives browsers in a normalized 1000x1000 coordinate space with a core set of 18 coordinate-based tools or an expanded set that adds element extraction, find, set_element_value and JavaScript execution, and can return JSON matching a caller schema. n2 operates a full desktop through batched GUI actions plus bash and file tools; the SDK ships local Docker and Daytona examples, and Yutori MCP runs it on the visible macOS desktop, sending screen contents to Yutori. A Python SDK wraps the APIs, a CLI runs research, browsing and Scout tasks, and an MCP server with workflow skills exposes these tasks and computer use to coding agents. Scouts monitor the web on a schedule, and Delegate is a consumer agent meant to complete handed-off tasks independently. Yutori also publishes a computer-use leaderboards page compiling reported results for six benchmarks. The publisher describes its Online-Mind2Web figure as independently verified and its Navi-Bench v2 and Westworld figures as its own evaluations; capabilities, pricing and reliability were not independently tested.
summary: Yutori's web-agent platform: the Navigator computer-use model API (n1.5 for browsers, n2 for full desktops), task APIs for browsing, research and Scout web monitoring, and the Delegate personal agent.
